summary: V6.25.26 verification — P0 React crash on the Dashboard Reference (Cypher) page is FIXED, descriptors render cleanly with title/sub. All 13 V6.25.26 backend tests PASS (9 materials/encounters/roll-table-material + 4 marketplace-share + PDF export), plus 21 V6.25.25 regression tests still GREEN (34/34 total). Frontend Reference page Cypher tab confirmed end-to-end: CypherReferencePanel mounts, all 7 sub-tabs render, 14 descriptors load with genre chips, no console/page errors. Atelier deep-dive UI nav (Workshop crafting panel, Table Tools relocation, lazy-suspense) could NOT be verified in the browser run because the /app/campaigns/{cid}/atelier route bounced back to the landing in this session — main agent should self-verify via campaign card → Atelier subtab navigation.

integration_issues.flow: Atelier deep-dive (Workshop crafting service panel + Table Tools relocation + lazy-suspense)
integration_issues.issue: Direct nav to /app/campaigns/{cid}/atelier returned to the landing page in this automation run — could not click Workshop / Table Tools / References subtabs. Auth was valid (Reference Cypher tab worked in same session, materials/encounters/marketplace API calls all 200/422/409 as expected). Likely a route-guard or initial-load redirect when the campaign was just created via API and not via UI flow.

issues: ?system=cypher query-string parameter is NOT honored on initial render — page always defaults to BESM 4E and requires a click on the CYPHER SYSTEM tab. Likely systemId state is initialised from a constant, ignoring URLSearchParams. Minor UX gap, not a blocker.

action_items: Main agent: self-verify Atelier UI surface area by opening a fresh besm-4e campaign through the UI (Campaigns list → click card → Atelier tab), then click Workshop subtab and confirm crafting-service-panel + 3 add buttons render; click Table Tools subtab and confirm both AtelierWorkshop AND ReferenceEditor render side-by-side; click References subtab and confirm 'References moved' notice + 'Open Table Tools →' button.
Optional: honor ?system=<id> query string on Dashboard Reference page so deep-links from elsewhere in the app land on the correct system tab without needing a manual click.

Optional: investigate why direct navigation to /app/campaigns/{cid}/atelier (where {cid} was just created via REST) bounces to landing in incognito-style automation — may be a same-tab race between campaign-load and atelier-mount.
critical_code_review_comments: Reference.jsx descriptor fix is correct — `title={typeof d === 'string' ? d : d.name}` and the `sub={Array.isArray(d.genres) ? d.genres.join(' · ') : ...}` guard handle both legacy string descriptors and the new {name, genres} objects safely.

marketplace-share endpoint correctly enforces (a) license_attestation=true required (422), (b) paywall + price_cents>0 required (422), (c) one-listing-per-archive (409). Snapshot stripping of mongo `_id` and audit fields keeps re-forks clean.
Encounters Library /run + /complete + /clone state machine is solid (status transitions ready → running → completed; cloning sets cloned_from_id and appends ' template' suffix).
PDF export still streams real %PDF bytes (>500 bytes, content-type application/pdf) with materials + encounters + sessions present — appendix wiring is live.

test_v62526_materials_encounters.py uses the 'wrong' BASE_URL fallback shape (allows http://localhost:8001) — fine for local dev but noisy if env var ever drops in CI; consider `os.environ['REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL']` to fail fast as the system prompt mandates.

rca of the issue: P0 RCA — Cypher /reference?system=descriptors objects (shape {name, genres: [...]}) were being rendered directly inside <Card title={d}/> which threw 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {name, genres})'. Fix in Reference.jsx renders d.name as the title and joins d.genres as the sub-text (with string-fallback for legacy entries). Verified live: 14 fantasy descriptors (Brash, Charming, Clever, Doomed, Graceful, Impulsive, Intelligent, Mystical, Mysterious, Resilient, Stealthy, Swift, Tough, Vicious) all render with genre chips, no console errors.
